en.marketHeading: What is actually different about marketing in {city}
market: {city} skews older than any other major Canadian metro, and that has practical consequences most marketing advice ignores. This audience converts by phone far more often than by web form, reads more before deciding, and is less forgiving of a site that is hard to use. A campaign judged purely on form fills will look like it is failing here while the phone rings, which is why call tracking is not optional in a {city} account.

The economy is anchored by public administration, health care and education, with tourism on top and a small but real technology sector. That gives the city unusually steady local demand and a visitor cycle layered over it, so a lot of {city} businesses are running two demand curves at once and only budgeting for one.

Then there is the island. Your customers are not going to hop over to the mainland for routine services, which protects local businesses from Vancouver competition in a way that is genuinely valuable. It also means the natural market extends up-island rather than across the strait, and targeting that reflects that will beat targeting drawn as a radius on a map.

faq.q: Do you have an office in {city}?
faq.a: No. I am based in Toronto and work from home, so there is no {city} office and I am not going to imply there is. Everything is run remotely over video and email, which is how I run every account.

faq.q: Most of our customers phone us. Does that break the tracking?
faq.a: It breaks the tracking if nobody sets it up, and that is one of the most common problems I find in {city} accounts. Call tracking ties a phone call back to the campaign that produced it, so you can see the whole picture rather than the small part that filled in a form. In this market that single fix often changes which campaigns look profitable.

faq.q: Should we target Vancouver as well?
faq.a: Only if you sell something people will get on a ferry or a plane for, or something you can deliver remotely. For most {city} businesses the water is a real boundary and the budget is better spent up-island, where the competition is thinner and the customers are genuinely reachable.

Three hours, and it matters for meetings rather than for the work. I take {city} calls in your morning, which is my early afternoon. If you need someone reachable late in your day on short notice, say so up front and we will agree what that looks like.
Google Ads management is $1,500 a month plus your ad spend. SEO consulting is $1,200 a month. AIO consulting is $1,800 one time. No setup fees and no long contract.
